title: Auto-attendant vs AI receptionist: compare all four call options
summary: Compare voicemail, auto-attendants, AI receptionists, and human answering services. Build intake, Calendly booking, and human handoff with vendor screenshots, billing limits, and a complete test script.

contents.title: Auto-attendant vs AI receptionist: routing a call and handling a request are different jobs.
The “free” answering plan can still have paid booking and overages.
Write one call map before configuring any tool.
Keep voicemail when a dependable callback is enough; keep a menu when it saves a transfer.
Configure a narrow intake before connecting the calendar.
Prepare Calendly, then connect and activate the correct event.
“Your team” and a paid receptionist are different destinations.
A simulated conversation does not prove that booking or transfer works.
When a caller is answered but the work is missing, check the destination.
What we checked, and what still needs your test

findings: Comparison intent: routing versus handling, human destination, existing number, after-hours coverage, booking, complete cost.

publicSearchReview.excluded: No competitor ROI averages or unverified quality rankings adopted.

factualFindings.finding: The previous page omitted auto-attendant from the title and comparison table. The expanded guide explains all four options supported by the public search review.
Marketing lists capability; detailed Free help states $3 booking feature, and native Calendly requires paid account.
Extra Calls OFF default redirects call26; infinite answering not implied.
Connection and caller-type activation are separate; direct single event link needed.
Simulation cannot validate real calendar availability or complete handoff; controlled testcall needed.
Own-team and paid human destinations differ. Qualifying live-agent call $3once, external business transfer not classified as this add-on.

rubySelectedTier.limitation: Lower tier plus overages not priced; no equal-quality claim.
